title: ENFORCEMENT DECREE OF THE SUPPORT FOR VETERANS ACT
full_text:
CHAPTER I GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1 (Purpose) The purpose of this Decree is to prescribe matters mandated by the Support for Veterans Act and matters necessary for the enforcement thereof.

Article 1-2 (Veterans' week) Pursuant to Article 3-2(2) of the Support for Veterans Act (hereinafter referred to as the "Act"), the State and local governments may conduct the following projects during the Veterans' Week under paragraph (1) of that Article:
  1. Commemorative events for Veterans' Week;
  2. Events to promote the employment of veterans, including job fairs;
  3. Commendation for enterprises, etc. certified as exemplary enterprises in employment of veterans, etc. under Article 16-2 of the Act;
  4. Other projects, such as events that the State and local governments deem necessary to enhance the self-esteem of veterans and improve social awareness of them.
  [This Article Added on Oct. 19, 2021]

Article 2 (Procedures for applications for benefits) (1) A veteran discharged from mid-term service or long-term service (hereinafter referred to as "veteran discharged from mid- or long-term service") who intends to file an application for benefits pursuant to the main clause of Article 4(1) of the Act shall submit an application for benefits in the form prescribed by Decree of the Ministry of Patriots and Veterans Affairs to the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs, along with documents stating the details of the benefits to be received; provided, medical treatment with reduced or exempted medical expenses under Article 20(2) of the Act and the use of public facilities under Article 23 of the Act shall be deemed to have been applied for upon submission of the application for benefits, regardless of whether such benefits are specified in the application. <Amended on Jun. 25, 2008; Jan. 14, 2014; Oct. 19, 2021; May 23, 2023>
  (2) Notwithstanding paragraph (1), Articles 14(3),17,20-3,22(1), and 24(1) shall apply to applications for vocational skills development training under Article 13(2) of the Act, employment support, etc. under Article 14 of the Act, incentives for job changes under Article 18-2 of the Act, educational benefits under Article 19 of the Act, and loans under Article 21 of the Act, respectively. <Amended on Dec. 20, 2007; Jan. 14, 2014; Jan. 9, 2024>
  (3) Upon receipt of an application under paragraph (1), the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs shall determine whether the applicant is subject to the application of the Act, after verifying the period of military service of the applicant, whether the applicant has been excluded from the application of the Act under Article 25 of the Act, and other relevant matters. <Amended on Oct. 19, 2021; May 23, 2023>
  (4) Application documents under paragraph (1) may be submitted by electronic means through an information and communications network. <Added on Jan. 14, 2014>

Article 2-2 (Issuance of patriots and veterans registration cards) (1) The Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs shall issue a patriots and veterans registration card (including the mobile version of such a card; hereinafter the same shall apply) to a person determined eligible as a veteran discharged from mid- or long-term service pursuant to the former part of Article 4(2) of the Act.
  (2) A person who has been issued with a patriots and veterans registration card pursuant to paragraph (1) may file an application for reissuance of such card with the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs, in any of the following cases:
  1. Where the patriots and veterans registration card becomes unusable due to loss or damage;
  2. Where there is a change in any matter prescribed by Decree of the Ministry of Patriots and Veterans Affairs among the details entered in the patriots and veterans registration card, such as the name and date of birth.
  (3) The Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs may establish and operate an information system for the issuance, reissuance, management, and authentication of patriots and veterans registration cards. In such cases, the operating system commonly applicable to identity verification under Article 12(4) of the Enforcement Decree of the Electronic Government Act may be utilized for the issuance, reissuance, management, and authentication of the mobile version of patriots and veterans registration cards.
  (4) Except as provided in paragraphs (1) through (3), matters necessary for the issuance, reissuance, etc. of patriots and veterans registration cards shall be prescribed by Decree of the Ministry of Patriots and Veterans Affairs.
  [This Article Added on May 23, 2023]
  [Previous Article 2-2 moved to Article 2-3 <May 23, 2023>]

Article 2-3 (Issuance of certificates for veterans eligible for benefits) (1) Upon receipt of an application from a veteran discharged from mid- or long-term service who is determined eligible for benefits pursuant to Article 4(2) of the Act or from his or her bereaved family member, the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs may issue a document certifying that the relevant person is a veteran discharged from mid- or long-term service who is eligible for benefits. <Amended on May 23, 2023; Jan. 9, 2024>
  (2) Matters necessary for the certificates, the scope of bereaved family members, and other relevant matters under paragraph (1) shall be prescribed by Decree of the Ministry of Patriots and Veterans Affairs. <Amended on May 23, 2023>
  [This Article Added on Sep. 22, 2020]
  [Moved from Article 2-2 <May 23, 2023>]

Article 3 (Request for personal data) (1) The details of personal data that the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs may request from the Minister of National Defense or the Commissioner of the Military Manpower Administration pursuant to Article 7(2) of the Act means the following information regarding veterans (including those scheduled for discharge; hereafter in this Article, the same shall apply): <Amended on Sep. 20, 2022; May 23, 2023; Jan. 9, 2024>
  1. Basic personal information, such as names, service numbers, military occupational specialties by branch, and ranks (referring to ranks at the time of discharge, and referring to respective ranks in cases of at least 2 discharges);
  2. Information on military careers, specialties, and education necessary to support employment and business start-up;
  3. Other personal information necessary to support veterans.
  (2) Upon receipt of a request for personal data from the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs under paragraph (1), the Minister of National Defense or the Commissioner of the Military Manpower Administration shall notify the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs of the requested information unless there is a compelling reason not to do so. <Amended on Sep. 20, 2022; May 23, 2023>

Article 4 (Fact-finding surveys) (1) The scope of fact-finding surveys under Article 8 of the Act (hereafter in this Article referred to as "fact-finding surveys") shall be as follows:
  1. Matters regarding the household environment, such as household composition;
  2. Matters regarding awareness of the standard of living;
  3. Matters regarding preparation for old age;
  4. Matters regarding satisfaction with quality of life, social participation, etc.;
  5. Matters regarding awareness of policies to support veterans discharged from mid- or long-term service.
  (2) A fact-finding survey shall be conducted as a sample survey, through interviews, telephone surveys, questionnaires, online surveys, and other relevant methods.
  [This Article Added on Jan. 9, 2024]

CHAPTER III ASSISTANCE IN EMPLOYMENT AND BUSINESS START-UP

Article 14 (Occupational education and training) (1) A veteran discharged from mid- or long-term service who intends to receive the following educational programs for social adaptation or occupational education and training pursuant to Article 13(1) of the Act shall file an application with the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs: <Amended on Jan. 14, 2014; May 23, 2023>
  1. Educational programs for social adaptation: Education designed to assist veterans discharged from mid- and long-term service in acquiring the basic knowledge necessary for adapting to changes in their lives after discharge and for preparing a new life plan and seeking employment;
  2. Occupational education and training: Training designed to assist persons who have completed education programs for social adaptation or veterans discharged from mid- or long-term service who possess the basic knowledge necessary for employment in acquiring higher job performance capabilities or developing knowledge and skills to adapt to technological advancements.
  (2) The Minister of National Defense may request that the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs provide educational programs for social adaptation and occupational education and training for persons scheduled for discharge from mid- or long-term service. <Amended on May 23, 2023>
  (3) A veteran discharged from mid- or long-term service who intends to receive vocational skills development training under Article 13(2) of the Act shall submit an application for such training to the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs. <Amended on May 23, 2023>
  (4) The Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs shall recommend a person who has submitted an application for vocational skills development training pursuant to paragraph (3) to an institution conducting vocational skills development training under the National Lifelong Vocational Skills Development Act, as prescribed by Decree of the Ministry of Patriots and Veterans Affairs. <Amended on Feb. 17, 2022; May 23, 2023>
  (5) Except as provided in paragraphs (1) and (2), matters necessary for the details of education programs for social adaptation and occupational education and training, the selection of persons eligible for such education and training, etc. shall be determined and publicly notified by the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs. <Added on Jan. 14, 2014; May 23, 2023>

Article 15 (Standards for employment support and frequency thereof) (1) The standards for providing employment support to children of veterans discharged from long-term service under Article 14 (1) 2 of the Act shall be as follows: <Amended on Apr. 1, 2025>
  1. A veteran discharged from long-term service shall fall under any of the following categories:
  a. The fact that medical treatment for a disease is required for at least 6 months shall be verified by a doctor's written opinion or a medical certificate;
  b. The veteran has any of the mental or physical disabilities specified in the disability classifications for persons with disabilities in Appendix 2 of the Enforcement Decree of the Act on the Honorable Treatment of and Support for Persons of Distinguished Service to the State, or falls under the category of persons with serious disabilities under Article 4 of the Enforcement Decree of the Act on the Employment Promotion and Vocational Rehabilitation of Persons with Disabilities;
  2. A child designated by a veteran discharged from long-term service shall not exceed 39 years of age as of the date the child submits an application for employment pursuant to Article 17 (1).
  (2) The total number of times employment support may be provided to persons entitled to employment support under Article 14(1) of the Act (hereinafter referred to as "persons entitled to employment support") shall be 3, aggregating the number of times employment support is provided to the persons specified in the subparagraphs of that paragraph.
  (3) If a veteran discharged from long-term service designates one of his or her children as a person entitled to employment support pursuant to Article 14(1)2 of the Act, the veteran shall submit an application for designated employment in the form prescribed by Decree of the Ministry of Patriots and Veterans Affairs, to the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs. <Amended on May 23, 2023>
  (4) If a child designated as a person entitled to employment support pursuant to Article 14(1)2 of the Act falls under any of the following categories, the relevant veteran discharged from long-term service may reassign the designation of a person entitled to employment support:
  1. If the child is dead;
  2. Where the child falls under any category specified in the items of paragraph (1)1.
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Oct. 19, 2021]

Article 16 (Preferential employment by State agencies and employment orders) The provisions of Articles 47,50 through 55,60,61, and 61-2 of the Enforcement Decree of the Act on the Honorable Treatment of and Support for Persons of Distinguished Service to the State shall apply mutatis mutandis to employment support for veterans discharged from long-term service and their children. <Amended on Jun. 25, 2008; Jan. 14, 2014>

Article 17 (Application for jog seeking) (1) If a person entitled to employment support under Article 14(1) of the Act intends to receive employment support, the person shall submit an application for job seeking in the form prescribed by Decree of the Ministry of Patriots and Veterans Affairs, to the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs. <Amended on Jun. 25, 2008; Jan. 14, 2014; May 23, 2023>
  (2) A person who intends to receive support for career and job counseling, job placement services, and other relevant services pursuant to Article 14(3) of the Act shall file an application for such support with the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs. <Amended on Jan. 14, 2014; May 23, 2023>
  [Title Amended on Jan. 14, 2014]

Article 17-2 Deleted. <Oct. 19, 2021>

Article 17-3 Deleted. <Oct. 19, 2021>

Article 17-4 Deleted. <Oct. 19, 2021>

Article 18 (Scope of specific type of jobs) The scope of the types of jobs suitable for the employment of veterans discharged from long-term service under Article 15(2) of the Act shall be as follows: <Amended on Jun. 25, 2008; Sep. 20, 2022; May 23, 2023>
  1. The types of jobs related to security, bodyguarding, and guarding services in institutions providing employment support under Article 30 of the Act on the Honorable Treatment of and Support for Persons of Distinguished Service to the State;
  2. The types of jobs designated by the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs, which are those in research facilities related to national defense and security or in defense contractors defined in subparagraph 9 of Article 3 of the Defense Acquisition Program Act.

Article 19 (Extension of maximum age for applications) Pursuant to Article 16(1) of the Act, the maximum age for veterans applying for employment examinations shall be extended as follows:
  1. Veterans discharged from military service after completing at least 2 years of service: An extension of 3 years in age;
  2. Veterans discharged from military service after completing at least 1 year but not more than 2 years of service: An extension of 2 years in age;
  3. Veterans discharged from military service after completing less than 1 year of service: An extension of 1 year in age.

Article 19-2 (Certification of exemplary enterprises in employment of veterans) (1) An enterprise or a public institution under Act on the Management of Public Institutions (hereinafter referred to as "enterprise") that intends to be certified as an exemplary enterprise, etc. in the employment of veterans under Article 16-2(1) of the Act (hereinafter referred to as "certification of an exemplary enterprise in employment") shall meet all of the following requirements:
  1. The number of employees who are veterans discharged from mid- or long-term service shall be maintained at a minimum of 5 for 6 months prior to the date of application for certification under paragraph (2);
  2. Employment security shall be deemed stable, taking into consideration the average period of service, etc. of employees who are veterans discharged from mid- or long-term service;
  3. The managers of the enterprise, etc. shall be deemed to have the intention to employ and foster veterans discharged from mid- or long-term service;
  4. The management of the enterprise, etc. shall be conducted in a sound manner.
  (2) An enterprise, etc. that intends to obtain certification of an exemplary enterprise, etc. in employment shall submit an application in the form prescribed by Decree of the Ministry of Patriots and Veterans Affairs, to the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs, along with the following documents: <Amended on May 23, 2023>
  1. Employment performance and status of veterans by enterprises, etc.;
  2. A document verifying the soundness of business management, such as a credit assessment report issued by a credit information company defined in subparagraph 5 of Article 2 of the Credit Information Use and Protection Act;
  3. Other documents verifying that the enterprise, etc. meet the requirements for certification specified in the subparagraphs of paragraph (1).
  (3) Upon receipt of an application under paragraph (2), the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs shall verify the relevant business registration certificate (referring to the certificate without the resident registration number excluded; hereafter in this paragraph, the same shall apply) through administrative data matching under Article 36(1) of the Electronic Government Act; provided, if the relevant applicant does not consent to verification of the business registration certificate, the Minister shall require the applicant to attach the certificate. <Amended on May 23, 2023; Apr. 23, 2024>
  (4) If an enterprise, etc. which have applied for certification pursuant to paragraph (2) meet the requirements specified in paragraph (1), the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs shall issue a certification as an exemplary enterprise, etc. in employment in the form prescribed by Decree of the Ministry of Patriots and Veterans Affairs to the applicant. <Amended on May 23, 2023>
  (5) The term of validity for certification as an exemplary enterprise, etc. in employment shall be 3 years from the date of the certification.
  (6) If an enterprise, etc. that have obtained certification as an exemplary enterprise, etc. in employment file an application for an extension of the term of validity under paragraph (5) before its expiration, the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs may extend the period only once by up to 1 year. <Added on May 28, 2024>
  (7) If an enterprise, etc. which have been issued with a certification as an exemplary enterprise, etc. in employment pursuant to paragraph (4) fall under any of the following categories, such enterprise, etc. may file an application for reissuance of a certification as an exemplary enterprise, etc. in employment in the form prescribed by Decree of the Ministry of Patriots and Veterans Affairs, along with documents verifying the grounds for reissuance: <Amended on May 23, 2023; May 28, 2024>
  1. If the certificate is lost or becomes worn and unusable;
  2. If any matter stated in the certificate is modified.
  (8) Except as provided in paragraphs (1) through (7), matters necessary for the requirements, procedures, methods, etc. for the certification as an exemplary enterprise, etc. in employment shall be determined and publicly notified by the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs. <Amended on May 23, 2023; May 28, 2024>
  [This Article Added on Oct. 19, 2021]

Article 20 (Support for business start-up) If a person intends to receive counseling or education for business start-up pursuant to Article 17 of the Act, the person shall file an application for such counseling or education with the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs. <Amended on Jun. 25, 2008; May 23, 2023>

Article 20-2 (Proactive job-seeking activities) "Proactive job-seeking activities prescribed by Presidential Decree" in the main clause, with the exception of the subparagraphs, of Article 18-2(2) of the Act means any of the following cases: <Amended on Feb. 17, 2022; May 23, 2023>
  1. Where the relevant person receives occupational education and training, career and job counseling, counseling and education for business start-up, etc. provided by the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs;
  2. Where the relevant person has been registered as a job seeker at an employment security office under the Employment Security Act and is receiving job placement services, vocational guidance, etc.;
  3. Where the relevant person is attending a course for employment or business start-up at a vocational skills development training establishment under the National Lifelong Vocational Skills Development Act or at a private teaching institute, etc. under the Act on the Establishment and Operation of Private Teaching Institutes and Extracurricular Lessons;
  4. Where the relevant person visits a job offer agency or applies for a job offer by mail, on the Internet, or through other means;
  5. Where the relevant person participates in an employment-related event and has an interview, etc. with a hiring employer;
  6. Cases similar to those specified in subparagraphs 1 through 5, which are determined and publicly notified by the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs.
  [This Article Added on Dec. 20, 2007]

Article 20-3 (Application for incentives for job changes) (1) A person who intends to receive an incentive for a job change pursuant to Article 18-2(6) of the Act (including those who file a reapplication after the payment of such incentive has been suspended pursuant to Article 20-5) shall submit an application for such payment in the form prescribed by Decree of the Ministry of Patriots and Veterans Affairs to the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs. <Amended on May 23, 2023>
  (2) Upon receipt of an application for the payment of an incentive for a job change under paragraph (1), the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs shall determine whether the applicant is eligible for such payment within 25 days and shall notify the applicant of the result. <Amended on May 23, 2023>
  (3) The Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs may verify proactive job-seeking activities under Article 20-2 at least once a month for a person who has submitted an application for the payment of an incentive for a job change and for a person who has received such incentive and may request the applicant to submit relevant materials, if deemed necessary. <Amended on May 23, 2023>
  (4) The Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs shall pay the incentive for a job change corresponding for the period during which proactive job-seeking activities are verified pursuant to paragraph (3) by depositing the amount into the account of a financial institution designated by a person eligible for such incentive on the 25th day of each month (or the preceding day, in cases of Saturdays or holidays). <Amended on May 23, 2023>
  (5) Notwithstanding paragraph (4), the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs may separately determine the date for the payment of an incentive for a job change in cases of special circumstances, such as a natural disaster, a calamity, or any other similar event. <Amended on May 23, 2023>
  [This Article Added on Dec. 20, 2007]

Article 20-4 (Amount of incentives for job changes) (1) The amount of the incentive for a job change to be paid to a veteran discharged from mid- or long-term service pursuant to Article 18-2(1),(3), and (6) of the Act shall be as follows: <Amended on Jun. 30, 2014; Jan. 13, 2022; Sep. 20, 2022; Jan. 12, 2024; Jan. 14, 2025>
  1. A veteran discharged from long-term service: 810,000 won per month;
  2. A veteran discharged from mid-term service: 580,000 won per month.
  (2) A person who intends to receive an incentive for a job change in a lump sum pursuant to Article 18-2(3) of the Act shall submit an application for the payment of employment (or business start-up) benefits in a lump sum in the form prescribed by Decree of the Ministry of Patriots and Veterans Affairs, along with documents evidencing his or her employment or business start-up, to the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs. <Amended on May 23, 2023>
  [This Article Added on Dec. 20, 2007]

Article 20-5 (Suspension of payment of incentives for job changes) (1) The Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs shall provide prior notification to a person who falls under the category specified in Article 18-3(1)1 of the Act that the payment of an incentive for a job change may be suspended. <Amended on May 23, 2023>
  (2) If a person in receipt of notification under paragraph (1) fails to proactively engage in job-seeking activities within 14 days from the date of receipt, the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs shall determine to suspend the payment of an incentive for a job change and shall notify the person of the grounds for such suspension, etc. <Amended on May 23, 2023>
  [This Article Added on Dec. 20, 2007]

Article 20-6 (Exceptions to suspension of payment of incentives for job changes) (1) "Cause prescribed by Presidential Decree" in the proviso of Article 18-3(1)1 of the Act means any of the following:
  1. The person's disease or injury;
  2. The person's pregnancy or childbirth;
  3. A natural disaster.
  (2) If a person who intends to receive an incentive for a job change is unable to proactively engage in job-seeking activities due to any cause specified to in the subparagraphs of paragraph (1), the person shall submit evidentiary materials, such as a medical certificate, to the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs. <Amended on May 23, 2023>
  [This Article Added on Dec. 20, 2007]

Article 20-7 (Recovery of incentives for job changes) (1) If a cause for the recovery of an incentive for a job change arises pursuant to Article 18-3(2) of the Act, the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs shall send a notice for the return of the incentive already paid to the recipient. In such cases, the return period shall not exceed 30 days. <Amended on May 23, 2023>
  (2) The Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs shall issue a demand notice to a person who fails to pay the amount to be returned within the return deadline under paragraph (1) within 7 days from the expiration date of the deadline, specifying a payment period not exceeding 15 days. <Amended on May 23, 2023>
  (3) Upon receipt of a notice for the return or a demand notice under paragraph (1) or (2), a person shall pay the amount to be returned to a national treasury collection agency, and the head of such agency shall, upon receipt of the payment, submit a notice of receipt of such amount to the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs without delay. <Amended on May 23, 2023>
  [This Article Added on Dec. 20, 2007]

CHAPTER IV EDUCATIONAL AND MEDICAL BENEFITS AND LOANS

Article 21 (Persons eligible for educational benefits and their scope) (1) The standards for providing educational benefits to a veteran discharged from long-term service or his or her child under Article 19 of the Act shall be as follows; provided, if such veteran or his or her child eligible for educational benefits has an academic background equal to or higher than the level of educational benefits to be provided, such educational benefits shall not be granted: <Amended on Jan. 14, 2014; Oct. 19, 2021; May 23, 2023>
  1. A veteran discharged from long-term service: If the veteran is admitted to a school specified in subparagraphs 1 through 6 of Article 2 of the Higher Education Act or in any school equivalent thereto (excluding graduate schools and graduate universities under Articles 29-2(1) and 30 of that Act; hereinafter referred to as "university") within 3 years from the date of discharge;
  2. A child of a veteran discharged from long-term service: If all of the following criteria are met:
  a. If the child meets the standards determined and publicly notified by the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs in consideration of the standard living expenses for the general public, fluctuations in wages and prices in the private sector, and other relevant factors;
  b. If the child attends a high school, technical high school, or any school equivalent thereto under Article 2 of the Elementary and Secondary Education Act.
  (2) The scope of educational benefits under paragraph (1) shall be as follows: <Amended on Jan. 14, 2014; Sep. 22, 2020; Oct. 19, 2021>
  1. A veterans discharged from long-term service: A subsidy for 50/100 of the total admission and tuition fees shall be granted from the National Treasury; in such cases, if the admission and tuition fees have been reduced, exempted, or provided as a subsidy under other statutes or regulations, the aggregate of the amount reduced, exempted, or provided as a subsidy and the subsidy specified in the former part shall not exceed the total amount of the admission and tuition fees;
  2. A child of a veteran discharged from long-term service: A subsidy for the total admission and tuition fees shall be granted from the National Treasury; in such cases, if the admission and tuition fees have been reduced, exempted, or provided as a subsidy under other statutes or regulations, the aggregate of the amount reduced, exempted, or provided as a subsidy and the subsidy specified in the former part shall not exceed the total admission and tuition fees.
  (3) A subsidy for admission and tuition fees under paragraph (2) shall be granted within a prescribed period of study prescribed by education-related statutes and regulations or the school regulations of the relevant educational institution; provided, if a person eligible for educational benefits is admitted, readmitted, specially admitted, or transferred to the relevant or another educational institution, subsidies for admission and tuition fees shall be granted for the remaining prescribed period of study at the current school, excluding the prescribed period of study for which a subsidy was already granted at a former school. <Amended on Apr. 17, 2012; Jan. 14, 2014; Sep. 22, 2020; Oct. 19, 2021>
  [Title Amended on Oct. 19, 2021]

Article 22 (Procedures for subsidization of admission fees) (1) If a person eligible for educational benefits under Article 19 of the Act intends to receive a subsidy for admission and tuition fees, the person shall submit an application for educational benefits to the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs, along with documents, as prescribed by Decree of the Ministry of Patriots and Veterans Affairs. <Amended on Jun. 25, 2008; Apr. 17, 2012; Jan. 14, 2014; Sep. 22, 2020; Oct. 19, 2021; May 23, 2023>
  (2) Upon receipt of an application for a subsidy for admission and tuition fees under paragraph (1), the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs shall issue a certificate of eligibility for educational benefits to a person eligible for such benefits, and the eligible person shall submit the certificate to the head of the school that the person attends (including a school to which the person is scheduled to be admitted; hereinafter the same shall apply). <Amended on Apr. 17, 2012; Sep. 22, 2020; May 23, 2023>
  (3) The head of a school in receipt of a certificate of eligibility for educational benefits under paragraph (2) shall request the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs to pay the admission and tuition fees for persons eligible for educational benefits, and the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs in receipt of such request shall, after verifying the relevant facts, pay the admission fees and tuition fees to the head of the school that the eligible persons attend, in lieu of granting subsidies for the admission and tuition fees to such persons. <Amended on Apr. 17, 2012; Sep. 22, 2020; May 23, 2023>
  (4) If a person eligible for educational benefits falls under the proviso, with the exception of the subparagraphs, of Article 21(1) or Article 19(3) of the Act, the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs shall suspend the payment of the admission and tuition fees under paragraph (3) and shall recover the amount paid in duplicate. <Amended on Apr. 17, 2012; Sep. 22, 2020; May 23, 2023>
  (5) In cases of changes in enrollment status of a person eligible for educational benefits, such as expulsion, suspension, leave of absence, or re-enrollment, the head of a college or university, a high school under the Elementary and Secondary Education Act, or a school equivalent thereto shall provide notification of changes in school attendance to the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs within 10 days from the date on which such change occurs. <Amended on Oct. 19, 2021; May 23, 2023>
  [Title Amended on Apr. 17, 2012]

Article 22-2 (Scope of financial information) (1) "Data or information prescribed by Presidential Decree" in Article 19-2(1)1 of the Act means the following data or information:
  1. Demand deposits, such as ordinary deposits, savings accounts, and free savings accounts: The average balance within the last 3 months;
  2. Savings deposits, such as term deposits, term installment deposits, and term savings deposits: The balance or total amount of deposits;
  3. Shares, beneficiary certificates, investments, equity stakes, and real estate (annuity) trusts: The final market value; in such cases, Article 54(1) of the Enforcement Decree of the Inheritance Tax and Gift Tax Act shall apply mutatis mutandis to the valuation of unlisted shares;
  4. Bonds, bills, checks, certificates of debenture, certificates of preemptive right to new stocks, and certificates of deposit: The face value;
  5. Pension savings: The amount paid regularly or the final balance.
  (2) "Data or information prescribed by Presidential Decree" in Article 19-2(1)2 of the Act means the following data or information:
  1. Loan status and details of arrearage;
  2. Unpaid credit card amount.
  (3) "Data or information prescribed by Presidential Decree" in Article 19-2(1)3 of the Act means the following data or information:
  1. Insurance policies: The refund payable upon contract termination or the insurance benefits paid within the most recent year;
  2. Pension insurance: The refund payable upon contract termination or the regularly paid amount.
  (4) Matters necessary for submitting documents confirming consent to provide financial information under paragraph (1), credit information under paragraph (2), and insurance information under paragraph (3) (hereinafter referred to as "financial information, etc.") shall be prescribed by Decree of the Ministry of Patriots and Veterans Affairs. <Amended on May 23, 2023>
  [This Article Added on Oct. 19, 2021]

Article 22-3 (Request for and provision of financial information) (1) When the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs requests the head of a financial company, etc. (referring to a financial company defined in subparagraph 1 of article 2 of the Act on Real Name Financial Transactions and Confidentiality and a credit information collection agency defined in Article 25 of the Credit Information Use and Protection Act; hereinafter the same shall apply) to provide financial information, etc. regarding a veteran discharged from long-term service who intends to receive educational benefits (hereafter in this Article referred to as "applicant for educational benefits") and his or her household members pursuant to Article 19-4(1) and (2) of the Act, such request shall specify the following: <Amended on May 23, 2023>
  1. The names and resident registration numbers of the applicant for educational benefits and his or her household members;
  2. The scope of the requested financial information, etc., the base date of inquiry, and the inquiry period.
  (2) If the head of a finance company, etc. in receipt of a request under paragraph (1) provides relevant financial information, etc. to the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs, the information provided shall include the following: <Amended on May 23, 2023>
  1. The names and resident registration numbers of the applicant for educational benefits and his or her household members;
  2. The name of a financial company, etc., that provide the financial information, etc.;
  3. The name and account number of a financial product subject to information provision;
  4. The details of the financial information, etc.
  (3) A request for the provision of financial information, etc. and the provision thereof under Article 19-4(1) through (3) of the Act may be made through the information and communications network of the association, federation, central association, etc. of which the relevant financial company, etc. is affiliated.
  (4) When the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs requests financial information, etc. regarding an applicant for educational benefits and his or her household members pursuant to Article 19-4(2) of the Act, the Minister shall request only the minimum financial information, etc. necessary to conduct an investigation to verify eligibility for educational benefits under Article 19-3(1) of the Act. <Amended on May 23, 2023>
  [This Article Added on Oct. 19, 2021]

Article 23 (Reduction or exemption rate of medical expenses for veterans hospitals) (1) The reduction or exemption rate of medical expenses for veterans hospitals under Article 20(2) or (4) of the Act shall be prescribed by Decree of the Ministry of Patriots and Veterans Affairs, not exceeding 50 percent of the medical expenses borne by the relevant person. <Amended on Jun. 26, 2009; Sep. 22, 2020; May 23, 2023>
  (2) Article 64-2 of the Enforcement Decree of the Act on the Honorable Treatment of and Support for Persons of Distinguished Service to the State shall apply mutatis mutandis to the bearing of expenses for prescription drugs by a person granted a reduction of or exemption from medical expenses for veterans hospitals or medical institutions pursuant to Article 20(2) or (4) or 20-3 of the Act. <Amended on Sep. 22, 2020; Oct. 19, 2021>
  (3) The reduction or exemption rate of medical expenses for entrusted hospitals under Article 20(4) of the Act shall be 50/100 of the expenses to be borne by the relevant person (excluding the expenses for prescription drugs under subparagraph 1c of Appendix 2 of the Enforcement Decree of the National Health Insurance Act) based on the burden rate for, and the amount to be borne by, the person, out of the costs of health care benefits under that Table. <Added on Sep. 22, 2020>
  (4) Notwithstanding paragraph (3), if the costs of health care benefits are to be directly borne by the relevant person pursuant to subparagraph 6 of Appendix 2 of the Enforcement Decree of the National Health Insurance Act, the medical expenses applicable thereto shall not be reduced or exempted. <Added on Sep. 22, 2020>
  (5) The criteria and scope of serious diseases under Article 20(5) of the Act shall be diseases specified in Appendix 1 among those which developed or worsened while the relevant person performed military service, resulting in the exemption from military service, etc. <Added on Jun. 25, 2008; Sep. 22, 2020>
  (6) The reduction of or exemption from medical expenses under the latter part of Article 20-3 of the Act shall be prescribed by Decree of the Ministry of Patriots and Veterans Affairs, not exceeding 50/100 of the expenses to be borne by a veteran discharged from long-term service or by a person discharged from military service after having participated the establishment of the Armed Forces of the Republic of Korea pursuant to Article 20(2) of the Act. <Added on Oct. 19, 2021, May 23, 2023>
  [Title Amended on Sep. 22, 2020]

Article 23-2 (Provision of prosthetic devices) (1) A person who intends to be provided with a prosthetic device pursuant to Article 20-2 of the Act shall file an application with the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs. <Amended on May 23, 2023>
  (2) Upon receipt of an application under paragraph (1), the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs shall provide a prosthetic device after verifying whether the device is necessary. In such cases, the types of, and standards for, the provision of prosthetic devices shall be determined by the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs. <Amended on May 23, 2023>
  (3) If a prosthetic device is worn out or broken and needs repair, a person provided with the device pursuant to paragraph (2) may request the repair from the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs. <Amended on May 23, 2023>
  [This Article Added on Apr. 17, 2012]

Article 23-3 (Details and methods of psychological rehabilitation services) (1) The details of psychological rehabilitation services provided by the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs under Article 20-4(1) of the Act (hereafter in this article referred to as "psychological rehabilitation services") shall be as follows: <Amended on May 23, 2023>
  1. Psychological counseling and tests;
  2. Arrangement of medical treatment, etc. at a mental health improvement facility defined in subparagraph 4 of Article 3 of the Act on the Improvement of Mental Health and the Support for Welfare Services for Mental Patients;
  3. Education for improving mental health;
  4. Other services prescribed by Decree of the Ministry of Patriots and Veterans Affairs, as deemed necessary for psychological stability and social adaptation.
  (2) A person who intends to receive psychological rehabilitation services shall file an application with the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs, as prescribed by Decree of the Ministry of Patriots and Veterans Affairs. <Amended on May 23, 2023>
  [This Article Added on Oct. 19, 2021]

Article 24 (Application for loans) (1) A veteran discharged from long-term service who intends to receive a loan under Article 21 of the Act shall submit a loan application to the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs. <Amended on Jun. 25, 2008; Sep. 20, 2022; May 23, 2023>
  (2) Article 69(2) through (4) of the Enforcement Decree of the Act on the Honorable Treatment of and Support for Persons of Distinguished Service to the State shall apply mutatis mutandis to determination, etc. on whether to grant a loan to a person who has applied for a loan pursuant to paragraph (1). <Amended on Jun. 25, 2008>

Article 25 (Maximum amounts of loans by type) The maximum amount of loans by type under Article 21(4) of the Act shall be determined annually by the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs, taking into account the financial resources available for loans within the following limits: <Amended on Dec. 20, 2007; Jan. 14, 2014; May 23, 2023>
  1. A loan for purchasing farmland: The appraised value of the relevant farmland;
  2. A loan for purchasing housing or a building site or for newly constructing housing: The appraised value of the relevant housing or building site;
  3. A loan for improving housing: Expenses incurred for the improvement;
  4. A loan for housing lease: The amount of the lease;
  5. A business loan: 30 million won;
  6. A loan for livelihood stability: 5 million won;
  7. A loan for school expenses: 10 million won.

Article 26 (Interest rates on loans by type) The interest rate on loans under Article 21(4) of the Act shall be determined and publicly notified annually by the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs within the range of 1.5 percent to 5.5 percent per annum; provided, the interest rate on any of the following loans shall be determined and publicly notified at up to 1.5 percent per annum: <Amended on Jan. 14, 2014; Sep. 22, 2020; May 23, 2023>
  1. In cases where a mortgage is exercised on real estate offered as security (hereinafter referred to as "secured property"), the unpaid loan during the period of exercising the mortgage;
  2. In cases where any unpaid loan exists as a result of the exercise of a mortgage on the secured property, such unpaid loan;
  3. In cases where a lawsuit for the return of a loan is filed against a person who provides a pension as security (including a pension under the Military Pension Act) or other security or who has obtained a loan with a guarantor, the unpaid loan during the period of such lawsuit;
  4. In cases where the repayment period is extended due to a natural disaster, a calamity, financial hardship, a disease, or any other similar cause or event, the unpaid loan during the repayment grace period.

Article 27 (Repayment period of loans) (1) The repayment period for each type of loan under Article 21(4) of the Act shall be determined by the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs within the following limits: <Amended on Jan. 14, 2014; May 23, 2023>
  1. A loan for purchasing farmland: 12 years following a 3-year grace period;
  2. A housing loan:
  a. A loan for purchasing a house or a building site or for newly constructing a house: 20 years;
  b. A loan for improving or leasing a house: 7 years;
  3. A loan for operation of business: 10 years;
  4. A loan for livelihood stability: 5 years;
  5. A loan for school expenses: 5 years.
  (2) If a person who has obtained a loan is deemed unable to repay the loan within the repayment period specified in paragraph (1), the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs may extend the repayment period by up to 3 years. <Amended on May 23, 2023>
  (3) Article 71 of the Enforcement Decree of the Act on the Honorable Treatment of and Support for Persons of Distinguished Service to the State shall apply mutatis mutandis to an application for an extension of the repayment period under paragraph (2).

Article 28 (Lump-sum repayment of loans) If a person who has obtained a loan has used the loan for any purpose other than the intended purpose, the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs shall not apply the repayment period specified in Article 27(1) and (2) and shall require such person to repay the principal and interest of the unpaid loan in a lump sum; provided, if a lump-sum repayment is deemed impracticable due to financial hardship or any other similar cause, the Minister may allow the person to repay the loan in installments within 3 years. <Amended on Jun. 25, 2008; Jan. 14, 2014; May 23, 2023>

Article 29 (Interest rate applicable to delayed repayment of loan principal) If a person liable to repay a loan pursuant to Articles 27 and 28 delays the repayment, the overdue interest rate determined by the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs shall be applied within the limit of the lowest overdue interest rate among those applied by banks under the Banking Act as of January 1 of each year; provided, if a loan is to be repaid in a lump sum or in installments pursuant to Article 28, this shall not apply to the principal of a loan for which the repayment period has not yet arrived under the original loan agreement, among the principal of the loan whose repayment has been delayed. <Amended on Dec. 24, 2008; Nov. 15, 2010; May 23, 2023>
  [Title Amended on Dec. 24, 2008]

Article 30 (Secured property)
Articles 76 through 84 of the Enforcement Decree of the Act on the Act on the Honorable Treatment of and Support for Persons of Distinguished Service to the State shall apply mutatis mutandis to secured property, etc. under Article 21 of the Act. <Amended on Jun. 25, 2008>

Article 31 (Preferential supply of housing) (1) If the State, a local government, or a project entity constructing and supplying privately constructed housing pursuant to Article 54 of the Housing Act (hereafter in this Article referred to as "housing supplier") preferentially supplies housing to be constructed or supplied, to veterans discharged from long-term service pursuant to Article 22(1) or (2) of the Act, the detailed procedures and methods for such supply shall be governed by the Housing Act.
  (2) If a housing supplier preferentially supplies housing to veterans discharged from long-term service pursuant to paragraph (1), the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs shall select eligible persons for such supply from among the applicants referred to in the former part of Article 22(3) of the Act according to the quantity of housing to be supplied and the criteria determined by the Minister, taking into consideration factors such as the period of non-homeownership and the standard of living, and shall recommend the selected persons to the housing supplier. <Amended on May 23, 2023>
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Apr. 30, 2018]

Article 32 (Use of public facilities) (1) The types of facilities that veterans discharged from long-term service may use free of charge or at a discounted rate pursuant to Article 23(1) of the Act and the reduction or exemption rate shall be as specified in Appendix 2. <Amended on Jun. 25, 2008; Sep. 20, 2022>
  (2) If a veteran discharged from long-term service intends to use a facility, such as an old palace or park, free of charge or at a discounted rate, the veteran shall present his or her patriots and veterans registration card to the manager of the relevant facility. <Amended on Sep. 20, 2022; May 23, 2023>
  (3) The Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs may recommend that the head of a local government grant discounts on the usage fees of parking facilities managed by the relevant local government to veterans discharged from long-term service pursuant to Article 23 (1) of the Act. <Added on Sep. 20, 2022; May 23, 2023; Nov. 25, 2025>

Article 32-2 (Procedures for legal aid assistance) (1) A veteran discharged from mid- or long-term service who intends to receive legal aid assistance pursuant to Article 23-2(1) of the Act shall submit a certificate of eligibility for legal aid issued by the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs to the Korea Legal Aid Corporation under Article 8 of the Legal Aid Act. <Amended on May 23, 2023>
  (2) A veteran discharged from mid- or long-term service who intends to obtain a certificate of eligibility for legal aid under paragraph (1) shall file an application with the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs. <Amended on May 23, 2023>
  (3) The Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs shall issue a certificate of eligibility for legal aid after verifying whether an applicant is eligible for legal aid within 10 days from the date of receipt of an application for the issuance of such certificate under paragraph (2). In such cases, the Minister may request that the Minister of National Defense verify whether the applicant falls under the category specified in Article 18-2(2)2 of the Act. <Amended on May 23, 2023>
  [This Article Added on Apr. 17, 2012]

CHAPTER V SUPPLEMENTARY PROVISIONS

Article 33 (Determination of eligibility for application of the Act) (1) "Employees prescribed by Presidential Decree who ordinarily engage in official duties for the State or a local government" in Article 25 (1) 4 of the Act means a person to whom Article 2 of the Enforcement Decree of the Public Officials Pension applies. <Added on Nov. 25, 2025>
  (2) If the Patriots and Veterans Entitlement Commission intends to deliberate and resolve on the eligibility for application of the Act of a person previously excluded from persons subject to such application pursuant to Article 25 (2) of the Act, the Commission shall require the person to appear before the Commission to express his or her opinion. In such cases, if the person submits his or her opinion in writing, he or she shall be deemed to have attended the Commission; if he or she fails to appear before the Commission on the designated date and time without good cause, he or she shall be deemed to have no opinion. <Amended on Jun. 25, 2008; Nov. 25, 2025>
  (3) When the chairperson of the Patriots and Veterans Entitlement Commission deliberates and resolves on matters regarding paragraph (2), the chairperson shall notify the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs of the result without delay. <Amended on May 23, 2023; Nov. 25, 2025>
  (4) The Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs shall determine whether the relevant person is eligible for the application of the Act within 20 days from receipt of notification under paragraph (3) and shall notify the person of the result. <Amended on May 23, 2023; Nov. 25, 2025>

Article 33-2 (Request for provision of data) "Data prescribed by Presidential Decree" in Article 26-2(1) of the Act means any of the following data: <Amended on Jun. 30, 2014; Dec. 30, 2014; Sep. 18, 2018; Apr. 28, 2020>
  1. Finance, national taxes, and local taxes; land, buildings, vessels, vehicles, and the right to sell houses; national health insurance, national pension, employment insurance, and industrial accident compensation insurance; the public officials pension, the accident compensation for public officials, the military pension, the pension for private school teachers and staff, and the special post office pension; details of global income and daily-paid workers' income; and other data on income, property, and employment status;
  2. Employment information, earned income subsidies, health and medical information, long-term care insurance for senior citizens, basic-type public direct payments, national basic living benefits, benefits for the second-lowest income bracket, medical benefits, basic pensions, pensions for persons with disabilities, and other data on protection and services provided by the State and local governments pursuant to statutes and regulations;
  3. Data regarding resident registration information, family relations certificates, immigration, military service, and correctional and other relevant matters.
  [This Article Added on Jan. 14, 2014]

Article 34 (Delegation and entrustment of authority) (1) Pursuant to Article 27(1) of the Act, the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs shall delegate the authority over the following matters to the head of a regional or district office of patriots and veterans affairs (referring to the Governor of Jeju Special Self-Governing Province, if the domicile or the location of the relevant school) having jurisdiction over the domicile of a veteran (referring to the location of the relevant school in cases of authority specified in subparagraph 7); provided, if the Governor of Jeju Special Self-Governing Province is delegated, the authority transferred to the Governor pursuant to Article 347 of the Special Act on the Establishment of Jeju Special Self-Governing Province and the Development of Free International City shall be excluded from the authority over the following matters: <Amended on Dec. 21, 2006; Mar. 27, 2007; Dec. 20, 2007; Feb. 29, 2008; Jun. 25; 2008; Apr. 17, 2012; Jan. 14, 2014; Sep. 22, 2020, Oct. 19, 2021, May 23, 2023>

  c. Receipt of applications for issuance of documents certifying veterans' eligibility for benefits and issuance of such documents;

Acceptance of applications for education or training, receipt of applications for vocational skills development training, and recommendation of eligible persons for such development training to institutions conducting vocational skills development training under Article 13 of the Act and Article 14 of this Decree;

Receipt of notification of the fixed number and employment of public officials in technical service, etc. by State agencies, etc., verification and inspection of the actual employment status by such agencies, etc., request for correction or supplementation from such agencies, etc., and receipt of notification of the results by such agencies, etc. under Article 33 of the Act applicable mutatis mutandis;
  c. Receipt of reports by enterprises, etc., requests by public officials under the relevant jurisdiction for explanations to ascertain the actual conditions of enterprises, etc., and instructions on requests for submission of relevant materials under Article 33-3 of the Act applicable mutatis mutandis;

  5-2. Deleted; <Oct. 19, 2021>

  b. Delivery of payment guarantee certificates, issuance of certificates of loaned property, acquisition of securities, entry of guarantors, acquisition of other securities, and approval for substitution of secured property under Article 56(1) through (5),(7), and (8) of the Act applicable mutatis mutandis;

  e. Deleted; <Dec. 21, 2006>

  12-2. Receipt of applications for the issuance of certificates of eligibility for legal aid and issuance of such certificates under Article 23-2 of the Act and Article 32-2 of this Decree;
  13. Determination of exclusion from eligibility for application of the Act or of eligibility for such application, and request for verification of criminal records under Article 25 of the Act;

  (2) The Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs may entrust the following business affairs to the Korea Veterans Health Service under the Korea Veterans Health Service Act, schools under Article 2 of the Higher Education Act, and other relevant specialized institutions, pursuant to Article 27(3) of the Act: <Amended on Jan. 14, 2014; Oct. 19, 2021; May 23, 2023>

Article 34-2 (Management of sensitive information and personally identifiable information) (1) The Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs (Including persons to whom the authority of the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs is delegated or entrusted pursuant to Article 34) may manage information on health under Article 23 of the Personal Information Protection Act and data containing resident registration numbers referred to in subparagraph 1 of Article 19 of the Enforcement Decree of that Act, if unavoidable for the performance of the following business affairs: <Amended on May 23, 2023>
  1. Business affairs regarding applications for benefits, etc. under Article 4 of the Act;
  2. Business affairs regarding the collection, management, etc. of personal information under Article 7 of the Act;
  3. Business affairs regarding fact-finding surveys under Article 8 of the Act;
  4. Business affairs regarding support for veterans under the Act and this Decree;
  5. Business affairs regarding suspension of benefits under Article 24 of the Act;
  6. Business affairs regarding the exclusion from eligibility for application of the Act under Article 25 of the Act;
  7. Other business affairs necessary to perform those specified in subparagraphs 1 through 3, 5, and 6.
  (2) If unavoidable for the performance of business affairs regarding the use of the operating system for the issuance, reissuance, management, and authentication of the mobile version of patriots and veterans registration cards under the latter part of Article 2-2(3) of this Decree, an institution entrusted with the operation of the operating system for identity verification under Article 89(2) of the Enforcement Decree of the Electronic Government Act may manage data containing information on health under Article 23 of the Personal Information Protection Act. <Added on May 23, 2023>
  [This Article Added on Jan. 6, 2012]

Article 34-3 (Re-examination of regulation) (1) The Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs shall examine the appropriateness of the scope of special occupational categories under Article 18 every 3 years, counting from January 1, 2014 (referring to the period that ends on the day before January 1 of every third year) and shall take measures, such as making improvements. <Amended on Dec. 9, 2014; May 23, 2023>
  (2) The Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs shall examine the appropriateness of the standards for employment support under Article 15 every 3 years, counting from January 1, 2017 (referring to the period that ends on the day before January 1 of every third year) and shall take measures, such as making improvements. <Amended on Mar. 3, 2020; May 23, 2023>
  [This Article Added on Dec. 30, 2013]

Notwithstanding the amended provisions of Article 26, if the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs granted a loan before January 1, 2014, the previous provisions shall apply to the interest rate on such loan.
Article 4 (Transitional measures regarding lump-sum repayment of loans)
Notwithstanding the amended provisions of Article 28, the previous provisions shall apply to a person who is subject to lump-sum or installment repayment of a loan or is repaying a loan in installments, as the person has violated the obligation to directly manage the loaned property or has used the loan for any purpose other than the intended purpose as at the time this Decree enters into force.
